archetype: Five-colour Dragon typal: accelerate, land fat fliers, and convert with per-Dragon entry triggers or an attacking-Dragon multiplier. The frame disagrees with the composition. strategic_frame.json declares 'combo' and deck-audit inherits it (tutors 4-8, protection 4-6), but the 99 holds 27 creatures, 24 Dragons, six narrow tutors, one contained combo line and zero two-card infinites. It is ramp-typal midrange being measured against a combo template.
verdict: Above the mana line this deck is in good shape and the pilot is right about it: 12 interaction copies, 6 protection, 6 tutors, 4 finishers, and — once the audit's own probe list is read — about ten real card-advantage cards rather than the five the taxonomy sees. What limits it is the mana, exactly as the captain's log says: 31 lands against a 36-38 floor, 43 sources against Burgess's 45, and a land-drop rate that falls 0.834 / 0.670 / 0.525 across turns three to five while 26 of the 68 maindeck nonland entries cost five or more. The colour half of that is misread by the headline: the audit's -15 is black, and black is the colour this deck barely wants. Red carries 53.9% of the pip load on 30.0% of the sources. Separately, and not what binds: the conversion is better evidenced than a stack count suggests and both declared kills shrank under audit. TWO checker-passed, non-withheld boards are lethal — stack 001 (255 damage, both opponents on its board dead) and stack 002 (64 damage in 12 instances, the 32-life seat dead) — and both are entry-kill boards. Meanwhile correcting two mis-declared groups moved THE ENTRY KILL from 0.481 / 0.356 to 0.240 / 0.153 and THE COMBAT KILL from 0.411 / 0.290 to 0.204 / 0.128, so the entry kill is now both the better evidenced and the likelier plan — and it rests on a three-card damage leg.

components.reading: Cost reduction is this deck's real acceleration — 24 Dragons in the 99 and a mana value 9 commander — and it is four cards: 25.8% of openers, 32.1% by turn three, 0.419 by turn six. Crossed with ramp, the turn-5-Ur-Dragon hand assembles 0.417 and only 0.285 by turn six.

One of the THREE components deck-audit flags thin — the others are the entry kill's three-card damage leg and, since the combat kill's multiplier group was re-declared, its two-card multiplier leg — at 13.7% of openers. It is also the component mana_analysis is blind to by construction: both add mana spendable only on Dragon spells, which land_colors counts as zero sources. So the -15 on colour-sources and this 0.306 are measuring opposite halves of 'can I cast a Dragon' and neither one alone answers it.

Seven Treasure sources, drawn 0.732 / 0.618 by turn six. Turning model_treasures on took the commander from cast-by-turn-six 0.0% to 4.1% and 'never cast in ten turns' from 9,175 to 7,170 of 10,000 while mean available mana stayed 4.219 at turn five — a Treasure does not raise your average mana, it buys the one expensive turn. Five of the seven are unreadable to the model, so every Treasure-derived mana figure is a floor.

Seven, 0.732 drawn and 0.617 by turn six — the corpus's 41%-at-seven line comfortably beaten, and the group correctly keeps all seven. Read its label precisely, though: it asks whether a Dragon entering does ANYTHING, which a draw trigger or a token answers. Only three of the seven — Dragon Tempest, Terror of the Peaks, Scourge of Valkas — turn an entry into damage. That is why the entry kill's damage leg is three and not seven, and it is the distinction the old declaration collapsed.

THE ENTRY KILL's damage leg, and the component that gates the deck's only rules-evidenced kill: three cards, 19.9% of openers, 25.1% by turn three, and one of the three components deck-audit flags thin. It was declared as seven until the declaration was corrected — Miirym and Lathliss are token MAKERS, not damage payoffs; Temur Ascendancy draws; and Garruk's Uprising matched a text scan only through its trample reminder text. Correcting it took the whole target from 0.481 / 0.356 to 0.240 / 0.153.

THE ENTRY KILL's multi-Dragon leg, and now the THICKER of its two halves at five cards, 31.2% of openers. The overlap I flagged in the first pass is gone, and it was the visible half of a worse defect: Miirym and Lathliss were also sitting in the damage leg, where neither belongs, and with that corrected they sit here alone. The target reads 0.240 assembled / 0.153 by turn six, and the gate is the other leg, not this one.

THE COMBAT KILL's multiplier leg, and the second mis-declared group this document has had to correct. It held four and two of them multiply nothing: Radiant Destiny is an additive anthem ('creatures you control of the chosen type get +1/+1', role payoff:typal) and Garruk's Uprising is trample plus two draw triggers (draw:engine, value:etb). Garruk's Uprising is literally the same card the entry kill's damage leg ejected last round, matched both times by its trample reminder text — one card, two text scans, two false positives, and I should have checked this leg when I checked that one. The leg is now Atarka, World Render (double strike on attack) and Thrakkus the Butcher (doubles Dragon power on attack): two cards, 13.7% of openers, and deck-audit flags it thin. Thrakkus also came out of the castable-Dragon leg, where he satisfied both halves of the target from one draw. The target fell from 0.411 / 0.290 to 0.204 / 0.128 — BELOW the entry kill's 0.240 / 0.153.
Eight, 0.764 drawn and 0.655 by turn six. Deeper than the payoff and the kill components — the deck is better at protecting the turn than at having one.

lean_into.what: Build toward the Dragon Tempest board and widen its three-card damage leg. lean_into.why: Two checker-passed, non-withheld boards prove this plan and none proves the other. Stack 001: fifteen Faerie Dragon tokens enter as one event, Dragon Tempest triggers fifteen times at X=17, and its final_state spends the 255 available damage to kill BOTH opponents on that board — engine-critic notes 255 also exceeds the 120 a full table of three fresh seats holds. Stack 002: one Lathliss cast under Miirym, Panharmonicon, Terror of the Peaks and Dragon Tempest deals 64 in 12 separately-targeted instances, killing the 32-life seat. Against that, no passing stack names any combat-kill multiplier — all six files grepped for Atarka, Thrakkus, Radiant Destiny and Garruk's Uprising, and none appears in any of them, withheld or not. When this was written the entry kill was 0.240 / 0.153 against the combat kill's 0.411 / 0.290 and I recommended it anyway on the evidence; re-declaring the combat kill's multiplier leg moved it to 0.204 / 0.128, below the entry kill on both figures. The recommendation now holds for evidence AND rate. What neither stack proves: 001 grants the payoff, the connection and an above-median d20; 002 grants four permanents already down and kills 32, not 40.

lean_into.what: The land tutors are already reliable — the basics question the pilot asked has a clean answer.
lean_into.why: Enumerated from the 26 land entries: Farseek has 17 legal target copies — eleven nonbasics (Blood Crypt, Breeding Pool, Canopy Vista, Cinder Glade, Hallowed Fountain, Jetmir's Garden, Overgrown Tomb, Sheltered Thicket, Steam Vents, Stomping Ground, Ziatora's Proving Ground) plus 4 Mountain, 1 Island and 1 Plains; Breeding Pool counts because it is Forest ISLAND, which I dropped the first time while correctly counting its Forest half elsewhere; Nature's Lore and Skyshroud Claim have 11 Forest-typed cards; Fabled Passage has 9 basics. Nature's Lore and Skyshroud Claim also put theirs in UNTAPPED, which is the tempo answer to half the pilot's third question. Nine basics carries the CURRENT package: dedicated demand on basics is at most three (Encroaching Dragonstorm searches up to two, Fabled Passage one), and Farseek, Nature's Lore and Skyshroud Claim all have nonbasic options ahead of a basic. The prescription below adds a fourth consumer — add_candidates[3]'s Prismatic Vista also searches a basic — taking worst-case dedicated demand to four of nine, while the swap holds basics at nine inside 36 lands rather than 31. Still comfortable, but I first wrote this conclusion without the card I go on to prescribe. So: raising the basic count is not needed for whiff-proofing, and Prismatic Vista should be judged on the flexibility it buys rather than on making the tutors safer.

The goldfish never casts the 9-mana commander in 7,170 of 10,000 iterations and reaches 5.428 mean mana by turn eight; a card at 8 is being paid for in slots and almost never in play. I am recommending this one knowing what it costs, and the corrected entry kill strengthens rather than weakens it: the target's mean assembly turn moved from 3.968 to 4.983, so the leg this card sits in comes together later than the deck can pay for an eight-drop anyway.
cut_candidates.cost_of_cutting: Re-derived against the corrected target rather than carried over. THE ENTRY KILL's multi-Dragon leg drops 5 to 4 — 31.2% of openers to 25.8%, arithmetic unchanged because that leg is not the one that moved — but the target it feeds is now 0.240 assembled / 0.153 by turn six instead of 0.481 / 0.356, so the same redundancy is being taken out of a plan half as likely to happen. The deck also loses the one CREATURE-token maker whose own tokens re-trigger it: Utvara Hellkite triggers on a Dragon ATTACKING, so the 6/6 Dragons it makes trigger it again. Enumerating all eight creature-token makers in the 99 (Ancient Gold Dragon, Dragonback Assault, Generous Gift, Lathliss, Miirym, Sarkhan Fireblood, Swan Song, Utvara Hellkite), no other compounds: Lathliss and Miirym are both gated on a NONTOKEN Dragon entering, which stack 002's final_state confirms by noting Lathliss's ability 'never fires here: every later entry is a token'. I first wrote 'every token maker in the 99', which was short by seven: the deck holds fifteen token makers and the other seven make Treasures. The conclusion is unaffected — no Treasure maker is re-triggered by its own Treasures, Old Gnawbone included, because its 'create that many Treasure tokens' is gated on CREATURES dealing combat damage and a Treasure is not a creature. The entry still holds, because the gate is the three-card DAMAGE leg and not this one, and because mana value 8 is nominal redundancy in a deck measured as unable to deploy it. The conditional I attached last round is void: I made it turn on whether the pilot took the entry kill or the combat kill as plan A, and the combat kill has since fallen to 0.204 / 0.128, below the entry kill. The entry kill is plan A either way, so this is its own redundancy being spent with nothing to fall back on. If the pilot would rather not thin the proven plan at all, hold Utvara Hellkite and drop the sixth add (Soul-Guide Lantern), the most optional slot in this document.

cut_candidates.why: Four mana that adds no board presence and no mana, in the deck whose binding axis is mana-base — 31 lands against a 36-38 floor, land drops at 0.525 by turn five. That is the argument that discriminates: this is a slot rather than an effect, on the axis that is costing games. I had also argued it is 'only good on a board that is already ahead'; deck-skeptic is right that this is not a test, because it is equally true of Dragon Tempest, Terror of the Peaks and Scourge of Valkas — the leg lean_into[0] tells the pilot to WIDEN. I have withdrawn it rather than kept it alongside the correction, and the cut now rests on the mana argument alone.
cut_candidates.cost_of_cutting: Re-priced, because my first version badly understated it. Stack 002 is not a marginal board: checker-passed, not withheld, its whole scenario is in the 99 today, and it deals 64 damage in 12 separately-targeted instances and kills the 32-life opponent outright. Panharmonicon is what the 64 rests on — it doubles every trigger in that cascade, because each one is caused by a creature entering. So this cut deletes one of the deck's TWO checker-passed lethal boards, not merely a ceiling, and my earlier phrasing ('the Miirym and Terror of the Peaks ceilings both come down') never said so. It is also the deck's only trigger doubler. What the record cannot settle is whether 002 is lethal WITHOUT Panharmonicon: Miirym would make one Lathliss copy instead of two and the cascade roughly halves against a 32-life seat, so this cut may cost lethality or only margin. open_questions[0] now names Panharmonicon as the permanent to remove, and one resolve-stack run on that board prices this entry properly. Until it does, the cut stands on the mana argument alone — the most expensive on this list by a distance, and a pilot who values the proven board over the land slot should hold it, which is a reasonable call rather than a wrong one.

add_candidates.why: Untapped red on turn one at one life, and untapped blue for Counterspell, Swan Song and Roiling Dragonstorm — U is 16 against a 22 target with nine land sources. It also taps for colourless with no life, which matters on the turns the deck is casting a generic-heavy Dragon.

citations.quote: Duke's judgment layer, in 60-card terms: 17–18 sources for a colour you won't keep a hand without, 14–16 for a main colour, 10–13 for a secondary, 4–7 for a splash.

add_candidates.closes: mana-base, and the basics-versus-fixing tension the pilot asked about
add_candidates.why: This is the direct answer to 'how many basics do I run'. It makes each of the nine basics act as any basic, untapped, for one life — so the deck gets the flexibility of more basics without spending more slots on lands that produce one colour. State the cost the other way round from how I first wrote it: it COMPETES with Fabled Passage and Encroaching Dragonstorm for the same nine basics rather than feeding them — all three search that one pool, and in the worst case Encroaching Dragonstorm's two plus Fabled Passage's one plus this one take four of the nine. Nine is deep enough to absorb that, which is why it is a cost and not a whiff risk.

add_candidates.closes: mana-base, and the engine's Dragon-restricted mana component
add_candidates.why: Names Dragon and taps for any colour toward a Dragon spell, untapped, and those Dragons cannot be countered. State the trade honestly: manabase.land_colors counts restricted mana as ZERO sources, so this moves the land count and the castability of 24 Dragons and does NOT move colour-sources. That is the same measurement gap the audit already flags on Desolation of Smaug and Sarkhan, Fireblood, and this deck already accepts it on Unclaimed Territory and Maelstrom of the Spirit Dragon.

add_candidates.why: Ranked last and optional — the pilot did not ask for it. It is here because the breadth measure only sees a card carrying the `hate:graveyard` role, and most graveyard answers do not carry it. Recomputed against (cards, roles): Soul-Guide Lantern takes interaction-breadth 4 to 5 and interaction 12 to 13, while Bojuka Bog, Scavenger Grounds, Relic of Progenitus, Tormod's Crypt, Grafdigger's Cage and Unlicensed Hearse all leave the axis at 4 — six tested, none moves it. Do not buy one of those six expecting the number to change. One mana, replaces itself later.

open_questions.question: Does either checker-passed lethal board survive being made from a NORMAL position, and does either kill a 40-life seat? Both grant the hard part. Stack 001 kills both opponents on its board but grants Dragon Tempest and Ancient Gold Dragon already down, combat damage already dealt, and a d20 fixed at 15 against a median of 10.5. Stack 002 actually CASTS its Dragon, which is the shape this question wants, but grants four permanents already on the battlefield — Miirym, Panharmonicon, Dragon Tempest, Terror of the Peaks — with eight lands, and its 64 damage kills the 32-life seat while the 40-life seat survives at 8. Resolve that same cascade with PANHARMONICON REMOVED — 002's exact board minus the doubler, which is the swap cut_candidates[5] proposes — and say two things: whether it is still lethal against the 32-life seat, and whether any version of it kills a seat at 40.
open_questions.why_it_matters: The pilot wrote 'the rest of the deck I am happy with', and the debrief recorded that as a disagreement with the artifacts. It is settleable rather than arguable, and the gap is now precise rather than general: the deck has two lethal boards on the record and neither has been shown to kill a fresh 40-life seat, 002 explicitly failing to. That is the difference between a deck that wins a pod and one that removes one player from it. It also prices a cut this document proposes: cut_candidates[5] removes Panharmonicon, and nothing on the record says whether that costs 002's lethality or only its margin.

open_questions.question: THE ENTRY KILL's damage leg is now three cards — Dragon Tempest, Terror of the Peaks, Scourge of Valkas — at 19.9% of openers, and deck-audit flags it thin. Is three enough for the deck's only rules-evidenced kill, and what in the pool or the format would join that leg? Re-measure with a widened leg against today's 0.240 assembled / 0.153 by turn six.
open_questions.why_it_matters: The previous version of this question is ANSWERED, and the answer was worse than this diagnosis guessed. I flagged that Miirym and Lathliss sat in both any_of groups and that _target_met therefore scored one card as satisfying both, making 0.481 / 0.356 an upper bound. That was the visible half of the defect. The other half: neither card is a damage payoff at all — both are token makers, in a group labelled 'a per-dragon damage payoff'. Temur Ascendancy draws rather than damages, and Garruk's Uprising matched only through its trample reminder text. With the leg corrected to the three cards that convert an entry into damage, the target fell to 0.240 / 0.153, the mean assembly turn moved 3.968 to 4.983, and the entry kill briefly became the thinner of the deck's two declared kills. That has since inverted again: deck-skeptic found the same mis-declaration in THE COMBAT KILL's multiplier leg, and correcting it took that target to 0.204 / 0.128, back below the entry kill. Three cards is now the number the deck's proven plan rests on, and nothing has priced whether that is enough.

open_questions.question: Re-goldfish the swapped list (31 lands to 36, five untapped or flexible sources in, six spells out) and report mean available mana at turn five (4.219 today), the turn-four and turn-five land-drop rates (0.670 / 0.525), and commander cast by turn six (0.041). Does five lands move them, and by how much?
open_questions.why_it_matters: This diagnosis prescribes five lands on the strength of an axis gap and a land-drop curve. The goldfish can price the COUNT half of that directly. It cannot price the colour or the enters-tapped halves, so a flat result would not refute the colour argument — but a flat result on the count would mean the five slots should be spent differently.

open_questions.question: What does the literature say about the floor on basic-land count for a five-colour Commander deck running Farseek, Nature's Lore, Skyshroud Claim, Encroaching Dragonstorm and Fabled Passage — and running Prismatic Vista alongside them, as this diagnosis prescribes — at what point does whiff risk become material, and how does that trade against generic fixing?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The pilot named this first of their three sub-questions. This diagnosis answers it by enumeration for THIS list — Farseek 17, Nature's Lore 11, Skyshroud Claim 11, Encroaching Dragonstorm 9, Fabled Passage 9, no whiff possible — but has no cited target to measure the nine basics against, and strategy.md's mana-base section does not set one. Include Prismatic Vista in the question: it is a fourth consumer of those nine basics, not a sixth searcher of the wider pool.

gaps: THE ORCHESTRATOR'S BRIEF WAS WRONG ON A LOAD-BEARING PREMISE, and it has since confirmed so. I was told 'three passing presentable stacks remain and none of them is a kill.' Stack 001 is checker-passed, carries no presentable: false, and its final_state kills BOTH opponents on its board — 'lethality confirmed' for the 30-life seat, and the 38-life seat as well; engine-critic has since found its 255 available damage exceeds the 120 a full table of three fresh seats holds. I used the narrower true claim throughout rather than the brief, and that claim still stands: no passing stack proves the deck ASSEMBLING and landing that kill from a normal board, because 001's scenario grants the payoff, the connection and an above-median d20.

colour-sources and mana-base are not recomputed by validate-diagnosis (they need mana_analysis), so the five land adds are argued from the tracked mana_analysis.json figures and from oracle text, not from a re-derivation. A re-run of mana-analysis after the swap is the check.

No deck_recon.json exists for this deck, so nothing here is grounded in what other Ur-Dragon lists run. Whether five colours at 36 lands is what strong lists do, and whether they solve red density with fetch-plus-typed-dual packages instead, is unanswered.

The enters-tapped half of the pilot's question is measured (5 unconditional, 9 conditional of 31) but not PRICED: the goldfish does not model tapped lands, so nothing in the repo can say what Canopy Vista and Cinder Glade entering tapped on nine basics costs in turns.

One logged game is texture, not a rate. Entry 001's Blood Moon lockout is the reason this audit was asked for and is not evidence about the mana base's normal behaviour — no figure in this diagnosis comes from it. The rates come from the 10,000-iteration goldfish, the counts from deck-audit and cards.json, the colour figures from mana_analysis.json, and the bracket from bracket_report.json.

engine.json was failing its validator with 39 errors when this diagnosis was first written, and I was instructed to cite no card list or figure from it. That state has moved: `validate-engine ur-dragon` returns OK today — 7 stages, 95 cards placed, 0 unassigned, 4 of 13 lines verified by a passing stack. The policy stands regardless and I did not revisit it, so the gap is real: nothing in this document cites engine.json, and the engine block above is built from deck-audit's priced components and goldfish_targets.json alone. A reader wanting the engine's own view should read the re-modelled file, not this block.

A PATTERN IN MY OWN REVISIONS, recorded because across four rounds it was this document's most reliable defect class: a correction lands at some of the sites that carry it and not all of them. Four instances. (1) axes[12] and lean_into[0] were rewritten and the `verdict` kept asserting the superseded ranking for a full cycle. (2) Farseek 16 to 17 reached axes[13] and lean_into[2] but not open_questions[3]. (3) The corrected axes[11] reading on which protection spells are free left cut_candidates[3] still saying 'two free ones'. (4) add_candidates[3]'s Prismatic Vista correction left lean_into[2] and open_questions[3] concluding from the uncorrected version. Every one was caught by grepping every leaf for the changed token, never by re-reading prose — two by me, two by deck-skeptic. Whoever revises this artifact next should grep for the figure or phrase they are changing before deciding they have changed it.

findings.note: THE VOLUNTEERED ENUMERATION IS NOT COMPLETE. The entry says 'Enumerating every token maker in the 99 (Ancient Gold Dragon, Dragonback Assault, Generous Gift, Lathliss, Miirym, Sarkhan Fireblood, Swan Song, Utvara Hellkite), no other compounds'. I regexed every oracle_text in cards.json for token creation: the set is FIFTEEN, not eight. The seven missing are all Treasure makers — Atsushi, the Blazing Sky, Cavern-Hoard Dragon, Goldspan Dragon, Old Gnawbone ('create that many Treasure tokens', which a 'create a/two/three' scan misses), Rapacious Dragon, Smaug the Magnificent and Smothering Tithe — and this document's own engine.components[3] is titled 'Seven Treasure sources', so it knows they exist. The eight listed are exactly the CREATURE-token makers. THE CONCLUSION SURVIVES and I checked it rather than assuming: no Treasure maker is re-triggered by its own Treasures — Atsushi is a death trigger, Rapacious an ETB, Smaug an upkeep, Smothering Tithe an opponent's draw, Goldspan attacks-or-targeted, Old Gnawbone a creature dealing combat damage (a Treasure is not a creature), and Cavern-Hoard counts artifacts the DEFENDING player controls, not yours. So 'the one token maker whose own tokens re-trigger it' is true over the full fifteen, and the nontoken gating on Lathliss and Miirym is confirmed by stack 002's final_state exactly as cited ('never fires here: every later entry is a token'). The fix is one word — 'every CREATURE-token maker in the 99' — and it matters because this repo has a documented history of a Treasure scoring as a body (goldfish's creature_body_count), so 'token maker' is precisely the term that has to be scoped here.

THE FOURTH SITE, and it is the same pattern a fourth time: a correction landing at one site and not at the two that draw the conclusion. add_candidates[3] was corrected THIS round to say Prismatic Vista 'COMPETES with Fabled Passage and Encroaching Dragonstorm for the same nine basics rather than feeding them … in the worst case … take four of the nine'. lean_into[2] still ends 'Nine basics is not the problem and raising it would trade fixing for whiff-proofing the deck does not need', and axes[13] still ends 'none can realistically whiff' — both enumerated against the CURRENT package, neither noting that this document's own prescription adds a fourth searcher of that nine-card pool. The enumerations themselves are right and I re-verified them: 9 basics (3 Forest, 4 Mountain, 1 Island, 1 Plains), Farseek 17 legal target copies, 11 Forest-typed, Fabled Passage and Encroaching Dragonstorm on the 9. The claim is true of the list as it stands and is stated without the qualification the prescription now requires. Compounding it, open_questions[3] routes research-strategy at 'a five-colour Commander deck running Farseek, Nature's Lore, Skyshroud Claim and Fabled Passage' — which omits Encroaching Dragonstorm, a basic-searcher this document names at axes[13], and omits Prismatic Vista, which it prescribes. The question that is supposed to set the basic-land floor is asked about a package the deck will not be running if the advice is taken. Fix: one clause in lean_into[2] ('and the sixth searcher this document adds does not change that, because …'), and name the post-swap package in open_questions[3]. No swap moves either way. (open_questions[3]'s '17 / 11 / 11 / 9' is separately correct — see my supported finding on it; this is a different defect in the same field.)

RE-JUDGED ON ONE JUSTIFICATION, as asked, and it holds. Removing the 'already ahead' test does not weaken the entry, because that test was the bad one — it condemned Panharmonicon on a property the entry kill's own damage leg shares, and lean_into[0] tells the pilot to widen that leg. Withdrawing it outright rather than parking it beside a correction is the stronger move: a rebutted argument left in place still argues. What remains is the argument I named in round 2 as the one that discriminates, and it is cited and measured — four mana that adds no board presence and no mana, against a binding mana-base axis of 31 lands versus 36-38 and a turn-five land drop of 0.525. Crucially the entry does not claim the mana argument SETTLES it. It states the unsettled half plainly ('whether 002 is lethal WITHOUT Panharmonicon: Miirym would make one Lathliss copy instead of two and the cascade roughly halves'), routes the exact run that would settle it, and blesses the opposite decision ('a pilot who values the proven board over the land slot should hold it, which is a reasonable call rather than a wrong one'). open_questions[0] now names Panharmonicon as the permanent to remove and asks both halves — still lethal against 32, and does any version kill a 40 — which is the run I asked for. This is the correct posture for a painful cut whose cost cannot be settled from the record, and it is last-ranked on a list the repo treats as ranked rather than mandated. What I am endorsing: an honestly-priced candidate with its decisive evidence named and absent. What I am NOT endorsing, and neither does the entry: that the cut is right.

The volunteered reversal is correct in direction and in arithmetic. I pulled Prismatic Vista from the corpus rather than memory — '{T}, Pay 1 life, Sacrifice this land: Search your library for a basic land card, put it onto the battlefield' (Land, colour identity empty, so legal and inside identity) — and read the two it is measured against out of cards.json: Fabled Passage searches 'a basic land card' and Encroaching Dragonstorm 'up to two basic land cards'. All three draw on the same pool, so COMPETES is right and 'feeds' was backwards. The pool is 9 (3 Forest, 4 Mountain, 1 Island, 1 Plains) and the worst case is 2 + 1 + 1 = 4 of 9, exactly as stated. 'Untapped' is right — Prismatic Vista has no tapped clause, unlike the other two. The card still moves mana-base, because that axis counts land copies in the 99 and this is a 32nd. See my lean_into[2] finding for the one place this correction did not reach.

'Two free ones' is gone and replaced by a pointer at the correction rather than a silent edit: 'Deflecting Swat and Flawless Maneuver are free only while you control a commander, which this deck rarely does, so the suite is deep on count rather than cheap.' That is consistent with the corrected axes[11] and with the oracle text. I also checked whether the correction undercuts the cut it sits inside, since it makes the protection suite look worse: it does not. The cut argument rests on the COUNT — six, the top of Zupke's 5-7 band — not on cheapness, and Eerie Interlude is not one of the six (deck-audit's protection list is Boros Charm, Deflecting Swat, Flawless Maneuver, Heroic Intervention, Miirym, Teferi's Protection; Eerie Interlude's role is `recursion`), so cutting it leaves protection at six. If anything the correction sharpens the cut: the deck wants cheaper protection and this is the three-mana one. cost_of_cutting still prices the real loss (the only recursion card, and the ETB re-trigger line), which I verified against card_roles.json in round 1.

Round-2 finding discharged: '17 / 11 / 11 / 9 targets'. I swept every '16' in the artifact and the remaining five are all legitimate — W and U source counts against their 22 targets, and three verbatim citation quotes containing '14–16', '12-16' and '37-39'. The Farseek figure is now consistent across all three sites that carry it (axes[13], lean_into[2].why, lean_into[2].evidence.farseek_targets = 17). The separate defect in this same field — the package the question routes — is filed under lean_into[2].

Round-2 finding discharged, and it re-ran the command rather than taking my word: 'validate-engine ur-dragon returns OK today — 7 stages, 95 cards placed, 0 unassigned, 4 of 13 lines verified by a passing stack', which is what I get. The claim is now past-tense and correctly scoped, the policy is intact and re-verified by me (nothing in this document cites a card list or figure from engine.json; the engine block reconciles to deck-audit and goldfish_targets alone), and it adds the right pointer — 'A reader wanting the engine's own view should read the re-modelled file, not this block.' That last sentence is the part that makes it a useful gap rather than a disclaimer.

Terminal check on the whole artifact for staleness, since three rounds of corrections is where stale text accumulates. Gate passes. Freshness re-confirmed: goldfish_metrics.json and mana_analysis.json both current on sha b544a740c197…, matching as_of_decklist_sha256, and the declaration figures in the document match the ones on disk exactly — THE ENTRY KILL 0.240 / 0.153, THE COMBAT KILL 0.204 / 0.128. I swept for every phrase this document has had to correct: no residual 'two free ones', no residual 'only good on a board that is already ahead', no residual 'one checker-passed resolution', no residual 'two components deck-audit flags thin', no residual Farseek 16, and every surviving mention of 0.411 / 0.290 or 'the LESS likely' is explicitly historical ('when this was written', 'has since inverted', an evidence key named combat_kill_before_multiplier_correction), which agents-common §9 permits and which is the right way to show a correction rather than bury it. For the record and not as a finding, since it sits outside this artifact: engine-critic's derivation that stack 001's lethal d20 threshold is 12 rather than 15 — 45% of rolls, not 5% — would make 001 markedly more reachable than open_questions[0] currently implies when it calls the fixed 15 'above-median'. Nothing the diagnosis says is wrong (the roll IS fixed at 15 in 001's scenario, and 15 IS above a median of 10.5), but a future round should read that threshold into open_questions[0], because it changes how hard the question is.
